rationale: Both candidates nail the central ground-truth concern (unscoped global default change validated only on Qwen-Image, affecting many CUDA diffusion models), with Y's model enumeration even more closely matching NumberWan's actual list. But X additionally hits the 'report pixelwise accuracy alongside latency' ask by exact test name, which Y misses, giving X higher recall. On precision, X's findings are backed by an auditable evidence-tagged methodology (grep/search_history/show_commit citations, with a transparent non-issue section for ruled-out concerns), while Y's 'What I verified' section makes suspiciously precise, unverifiable claims (exact local pytest pass count, matching bf16 diffs to 4 decimals across three kernel implementations) presented as fact without shown evidence — a fabrication risk that undercuts its Part 2 approval. Both are concretely actionable with file/line evidence; X also includes literal suggested-diff blocks.
